lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e3600–3200 cm⁻¹: O–H y:
"

3600–3200 cm⁻¹: O–H and N–H · ~3000: C–H · 2260–2100: C≡N and C≡C · 1750–1650: C=O · 1680–1600: C=C · < 1500: fingerprint. The (very strong) intensity of the C=O makes it the easiest peak to identify. Here: C=O of propanone (1715 cm⁻¹).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAldehído (≈ 1730 + C–:
"

Aldehyde (≈ 1730 + C–H at 2720/2820), ketone (≈ 1715), ester (≈ 1740 + strong C–O at 1240) and acid (≈ 1710 + very broad O–H 2500–3300). The group is determined by the set of bands, not just by the C=O.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eárea\:
"

The area of each signal (integration) is proportional to the number of H (ethanol: 3 : 2 : 1). The multiplicity follows the n+1 rule: an H with n neighboring H atoms (on adjacent carbons) splits into n+1 lines with Pascal intensities. CH₃ next to CH₂ → triplet; CH₂ next to CH₃ → quartet (J ≈ 7 Hz).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn \u003cb\u003eRMN ¹:
"

In ¹H NMR protons in a magnetic field absorb radiofrequency. The chemical shift δ (ppm, relative to TMS = 0) reflects the environment: electronegative atoms deshield and increase δ. Ethanol: CH₃ 1.2 · CH₂–O 3.7 · OH variable. There is one signal for each type of equivalent H.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la pestaña \u003cb:
"

In the Lab tab there is a mystery spectrum: the IR bands and NMR signals of a molecule from the library are shown; choose which one it is. Hint: start with the C=O band (≈ 1700), then the number of signals and the integration.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEtanoato de etilo: IR:
"

Ethyl ethanoate: IR with C=O at 1740 and C–O at 1240 → ester. NMR: singlet 2.05 (3H, CH₃C=O), quartet 4.1 (2H, OCH₂) and triplet 1.25 (3H, CH₃): CH₃CO–O–CH₂CH₃. The integrals are added up (8 H = C₄H₈O₂) and checked against the unsaturations: DBE = 1 (the C=O).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos enlaces vibran (t:
"

Bonds vibrate (stretching and bending) at characteristic frequencies. If the vibration changes the dipole moment, the molecule absorbs IR radiation of that frequency (wavenumber in cm⁻¹). In the spectrum it appears as a downward band (lower transmittance). Here: O–H stretch of ethanol (broad band due to hydrogen bonding).

"
